segments.narration: A fire under this town has burned since 1962. Sixty years on, nobody has found a way to put it out.
Centralia was a mining borough in Pennsylvania, sitting straight on top of worked-out anthracite seams.
On the twenty-seventh of May, 1962, the council burned the town dump. The flames found a coal seam through an unsealed pit.
Then gardens and cellars started venting smoke. In 1981 the ground swallowed twelve-year-old Todd Domboski, 46 metres down. His cousin hauled him out.
The state condemned every building in the borough in 1992. At the current rate, the seam holds enough coal to burn for another 250 years.

verdicts.claim: A coal seam fire beneath Centralia, Pennsylvania has burned since at least May 1962.
verdicts.note: 82% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article, including 1 number(s)

verdicts.claim: Centralia sat directly above worked and abandoned anthracite coal seams.
verdicts.note: The borough lies above anthracite mine workings into which the fire spread.

verdicts.claim: The most documented account traces the fire to a landfill fire lit on 27 May 1962 that reached the seams.
verdicts.note: The most documented theory is that the town council set a fire to clean the landfill on 27 May 1962, which spread to the underground mines.

verdicts.claim: In 1981 a sinkhole about 46 metres deep opened beneath twelve-year-old Todd Domboski, who was pulled out by his cousin.
verdicts.note: 1981: a sinkhole 4 ft wide by 150 ft (46 m) deep opened under 12-year-old Todd Domboski; his 14-year-old cousin Eric Wolfgang rescued him.

verdicts.claim: Pennsylvania condemned every building in the borough by eminent domain in 1992, and the fire could burn for over 250 more years.
verdicts.note: Governor Bob Casey invoked eminent domain over all properties in 1992; at its current rate the fire could burn for over 250 years.
